A global automotive OEM — Manufacturing & Industrial engagement delivered by a 31-person team over 20 months, Global scope, commercial model: build-transfer.

items: Legacy lines uninstrumented; OEE components estimated; changeover losses structurally accepted.
Quality escapes discovered at customer complaints; inspection by sampling.
Flat plant networks left lines exposed to ransomware.

blocks.x: We retrofitted sensor network on live lines (OPC UA/Sparkplug with data contracts), deployed vision inspection closing loops into andon/MES, and gave planners a Swarm scheduling assistant proposing changeover-aware sequences. IEC 62443 zoning preceded instrumentation — security first, then telemetry, then decisions on Forge.

The operating cadence, concretely: weeks 1–2 produce the signed baseline: current per production line performance, method note, and a control owner who co-signs every later claim. the middle block runs the pilot against live SCADA & historians data at deliberately small scope: one path, one team, one product line, expanded only after its eval gate holds. Nothing in this topology is accidental: every state change is replayable from the signed baseline for Manufacturing & Industrial at scale, so a regression is a cohort, never an estate.. The design principle here is simple: every state change is replayable from the signed baseline across Manufacturing & Industrial, which keeps the blast radius of any change inside one lane.
